name: Southern branch (Civil War, slavery)
description: Southern Presbyterians split from the PCUSA in 1861 and formed the PCCSA/PCUS.
narrative: Southern Presbyterians split from the PCUSA in 1861 over slavery and the federal union, forming the PCCSA/PCUS.

further_reading.title: History of the Church — Presbyterian Historical Society
further_reading.snippet: Formation and development: The national crisis over slavery and federal union divided Presbyterians as well as the country. Southern Presbyterians organized the Presbyterian Church in the Confederate States of America in 1861; the body later used the PCUS name.

further_reading.title: Westminster Confession and Catechisms — OPC official texts
further_reading.snippet: Teaching and practice: God’s grace and sovereignty: salvation is understood as God’s initiative in Christ rather than a human achievement.

further_reading.title: Westminster Confession and Larger and Shorter Catechisms
further_reading.snippet: Historic Reformed doctrinal and teaching texts. American revisions and each church’s subscription rules must be distinguished from the original Scottish form.

name: Conservative response to modernism
description: Conservative Presbyterians formed the OPC in 1936 amid the fundamentalist-modernist controversy.
narrative: The OPC was formed in 1936 as a conservative response to liberal theology and the fundamentalist-modernist controversy within the PCUSA.

key_figures.name: J. Gresham Machen
key_figures.role: New Testament scholar, Westminster Seminary founder, and leading organizer of the church
key_figures.summary: A New Testament scholar formerly at Princeton, founder of Westminster Theological Seminary, and leading figure in the 1936 Presbyterian separation.

further_reading.title: Our History — Orthodox Presbyterian Church
further_reading.snippet: Formation and development: Machen and colleagues believed modernist teaching had undermined the church’s doctrinal and missionary witness. Their conflict with the PCUSA produced a separate body in June 1936, first called the Presbyterian Church of America.

further_reading.title: Westminster Confession and Catechisms — OPC official texts
further_reading.snippet: Teaching and practice: Westminster subscription: the confession and catechisms are subordinate standards under Scripture.

further_reading.title: Westminster Confession and Catechisms
further_reading.snippet: The OPC receives an American revised form; its account explicitly distinguishes revisions it accepts from PCUSA changes it did not adopt.

name: Conservative response to liberalism
description: The PCA formed in 1973 as a conservative departure from the PCUS.
narrative: The PCA was formed in 1973; its founding assembly noted it was leaving the PCUS and gathered in Birmingham for its first General Assembly.

key_figures.name: W. Jack Williamson
key_figures.summary: A Presbyterian leader associated with the PCA’s founding generation. His inclusion concerns organizational beginnings rather than authorship of the whole Reformed tradition.

key_figures.name: Morton H. Smith
key_figures.role: Reformed theologian and founding stated clerk of the PCA, serving 1973–1988; distinct from Morton Smith the ancient historian
key_figures.summary: Morton Howison Smith was a Reformed theologian and the PCA’s first stated clerk (1973–1988), responsible for important early administrative continuity. He is a different person from Morton Smith, the Columbia ancient historian associated with the Secret Gospel of Mark debate.

further_reading.title: About the PCA — official description
further_reading.snippet: Formation and development: Organizers opposed what they regarded as theological liberalism and weakening commitment to biblical and Reformed teaching in the PCUS. They sought a church explicitly committed to Scripture, Westminster doctrine, and evangelistic mission.

further_reading.title: Westminster Confession and Larger and Shorter Catechisms
further_reading.snippet: Historic Reformed doctrinal and teaching texts. American revisions and each church’s subscription rules must be distinguished from the original Scottish form.

further_reading.title: About the PCA: purpose and government
further_reading.snippet: Official contemporary explanation of the church’s aims and Westminster commitments; self-description rather than independent proof of every founding allegation.

name: Ecumenical reunion
description: PCUSA merged with UPCNA to form UPCUSA in 1958.
narrative: The PCUSA merged with the UPCNA in 1958 to form the UPCUSA.

key_figures.name: Eugene Carson Blake
key_figures.role: stated clerk and advocate of the 1958 union
key_figures.summary: A Presbyterian stated clerk and advocate of ecumenical cooperation who helped advance the 1958 union creating UPCUSA.

key_figures.name: Samuel W. Shane
key_figures.role: UPCNA stated clerk and later associate stated clerk
key_figures.summary: The UPCNA stated clerk at the 1958 union, later serving as associate stated clerk in the new denomination.

key_figures.name: Theophilus M. Taylor
key_figures.role: first moderator of the new denomination
key_figures.summary: A former UPCNA missionary and seminary professor elected first moderator of UPCUSA, symbolizing the participation of both uniting churches.

further_reading.title: Stories from GA: 1958 Union — Presbyterian Church USA
further_reading.snippet: Formation and development: Union advocates sought stronger shared ministry across previously distinct Reformed institutions. Eugene Carson Blake promoted ecumenical cooperation, while some UPCNA members worried about losing their independent identity.

further_reading.title: Book of Confessions — official resource
further_reading.snippet: Teaching and practice: God’s grace and sovereignty: salvation is understood as God’s initiative in Christ rather than a human achievement.

further_reading.title: Westminster Confession and Larger and Shorter Catechisms
further_reading.snippet: Historic Reformed doctrinal and teaching texts. American revisions and each church’s subscription rules must be distinguished from the original Scottish form.

further_reading.title: Confession of 1967 / Book of Confessions
further_reading.snippet: A major expansion from a Westminster-centered framework to a historical collection of confessional witnesses.

name: Northern-Southern reunion
reasons: reunion of northern and southern Presbyterian branches
description: PCUS merged with UPCUSA in 1983 to form the PC(USA).
causes: reunion of northern and southern branches
narrative: PCUS and UPCUSA reunited in 1983 to form the PC(USA).

key_figures.name: James Costen
key_figures.role: moderator associated with the northern church at reunion
key_figures.summary: moderator associated with the northern church at reunion. This role should be read in the formation and development described above, rather than as a claim of sole authorship of the tradition.

key_figures.name: John Anderson
key_figures.role: moderator associated with the southern church at reunion
key_figures.summary: moderator associated with the southern church at reunion. This role should be read in the formation and development described above, rather than as a claim of sole authorship of the tradition.

further_reading.title: History of the Church — Presbyterian Historical Society
further_reading.snippet: Formation and development: The 1983 reunion sought to reunite major American Presbyterian streams divided since the Civil War era and to strengthen shared ministry. It joined institutions with overlapping Reformed ancestry but distinct histories.

further_reading.title: Confessions — Presbyterian Church USA
further_reading.snippet: Teaching and practice: God’s grace and sovereignty: salvation is understood as God’s initiative in Christ rather than a human achievement.

further_reading.title: Book of Confessions
further_reading.snippet: Constitutional collection of creeds, confessions, and catechisms from different periods; it is not a claim that every statement originated in 1983.

further_reading.title: Confession of Belhar
further_reading.snippet: South African confession addressing unity, reconciliation, and justice; received by PCUSA in 2016.
